parsed.answer: The evidence shows that SCNT embryos exhibit persistent H3K9me3/2 hypermethylation due to deficient expression of the H3K9 demethylases KDM4D and KDM4E at embryonic genome activation, and that overexpression (ectopic expression) of KDM4E removes this H3K9me3 barrier, restores the global transcriptome, improves blastocyst formation, and increases SCNT cloning efficiency. Thus removal of H3K9me3 via an ectopically expressed H3K9 demethylase does improve reprogramming efficiency in SCNT.
